clue.text: Composer of operas, including The Ring — his work is transporting

indicators.note: including means the composer's name takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: Richard Wagner wrote operas, among them the Ring cycle
a ring is round, so it is the letter O

explanation.surface: A note on Wagner's operas, with the Ring cycle singled out as his most moving work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Ring' looks like part of the musical description, but it only gives the round letter O to put inside WAGNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver of horse-drawn wagons spends his working life carrying people and goods.

clue.text: With that fellow it's just a passing fancy

parts.note: that fellow is him

explanation.surface: A remark that being with a certain man is only a fleeting attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden impulse or fleeting notion is the kind of fancy that passes.

clue.text: Pigment found in spongy ground in quarries

indicators.note: in means the soft ground goes inside the word for quarries

parts.note: quarries are hunted animals, game
a bog is soft, spongy wet ground

explanation.surface: A colouring found in soft earth at the bottom of stone pits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarries' suggests stone pits but means hunted animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow gum resin from Asian trees is used as a watercolour.

clue.text: For example, debt-collector raised elbow

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: EG is short for exempli gratia, for example
a dun is someone who demands payment of debts

explanation.surface: A debt-collector raises an elbow, perhaps threateningly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the whole run EGDUN upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow someone is to push or poke them with that joint.

clue.text: Way to divide one's foreign currency, primarily for the pragmatic

parts.note: the real is the currency of Brazil, and an old Spanish coin

indicators.note: to divide means the road abbreviation goes into the middle of the next piece

parts.note: one's reads as one is, I plus S
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A guide to sharing out foreign money, mostly for practical people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily for' is a loose link before the definition; 'to divide' puts the road abbreviation inside one's, and the foreign currency stands first.
explanation.definitionFit: People who deal with things as they really are, not ideals, are practical-minded.

clue.text: Engine cover is alarming new driver coming in

indicators.note: coming in means the learner's letter goes inside the word for alarming

parts.note: cowing someone is intimidating or alarming them
L is the learner plate shown by a new driver in Britain

explanation.surface: A nervous learner driver comes into a garage and is scared by the engine cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal hood fitted over an aircraft or car engine is called by this name.

clue.text: Daycare provider whose charges are small

definitions.text: Daycare provider whose charges are small

parts.words: Daycare provider whose charges are small
parts.note: read as a cheap nursery, but its charges are the little children in its care

explanation.surface: A nursery that does not charge much.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery where young children are minded while parents work.

clue.text: Resist having accommodation for spectators

parts.note: having means with, as in a man with a hat
a stand is the structure where spectators sit or stand at a sports ground

explanation.surface: A sports ground holds out against providing seating for fans.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold out against pressure or attack is to resist it.

clue.text: Ape — one's located it in China

parts.note: one is I; the 's (is) and located are links

indicators.note: in means the word it goes inside the word for China

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate)
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monkey has been found in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy or mimic them.

clue.text: Good old Aussie, one with potentially lucrative prospects

parts.note: taken as written
digger is slang for an Australian, especially a soldier

explanation.surface: An old Australian prospector is in line for riches.
explanation.walkthrough: Digger is a nickname for Australians; the definition literally describes a prospector, and slyly someone marrying for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone courting a rich partner for money has a lucrative prospect, as does a prospector seeking ore.

clue.text: One initially minded to intercede, with instant effect

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of minded is used

parts.note: to intercede between two sides is to mediate

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to step into a dispute does so at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that takes effect at once, without delay, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Birdsong gives us a buzz, as the Irish put it

indicators.note: as the Irish put it means the word is said in an Irish accent, which drops the H after T

parts.note: a buzz of excitement is a thrill

explanation.surface: Hearing the birds sing is exciting, says an Irish speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: A stage Irish accent says TH as a plain T, so THRILL comes out as the birdsong word.
explanation.definitionFit: A warbling, quavering run of notes sung by a bird is this kind of sound.

clue.text: Singular performance of Brief Encounter

definitions.meaning: a show put on for a single evening in one town only
a casual romantic or sexual meeting lasting one night

explanation.surface: A one-off screening of the classic British film Brief Encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: Brief Encounter is a famous 1945 British film about a short-lived affair, which steers the solver to cinema rather than to a fling.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both a touring act's single-evening booking and a short-lived sexual liaison.

clue.text: Italian citizen breaking into a plane

indicators.note: breaking means the letters of into a plane are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: An Italian forces their way into an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Naples, a city in southern Italy, is called by this name.

clue.text: Characters in event are agitated and exhausted

definitions.note: past tense of a verb; the answer is the base form of the same verb

indicators.note: agitated means the letters of the words event and are are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: People at some function are worked up and worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters in' points to the letters of 'event are' as the material; 'agitated' shuffles them.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain someone of energy or vitality is to tire them out completely.

clue.text: Confer Open University award in very secure environment

indicators.note: environment means the first pieces surround the next ones

parts.note: safe means secure
OU is the Open University, a British distance-learning university
CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award

explanation.surface: Presenting a degree from the Open University under tight security.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant or bestow something graciously is to confer it.

clue.text: Dreadful person best avoided by soldiers

definitions.text: Dreadful person best avoided by soldiers

parts.words: Dreadful person best avoided by soldiers
parts.note: read as troops shunning a villain, but soldiers are also the strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg, which should not be rotten

explanation.surface: A villain whom the army would do well to steer clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers are the British name for fingers of toast dunked in a boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotten person is called by the same phrase as an off egg, here one no toast finger should touch.

clue.text: In this case, the pulse is regular

definitions.text: In this case, the pulse is regular

parts.words: In this case, the pulse is regular
parts.note: read as a doctor's remark on a heartbeat, but a case is a pod and the pulse is the peas lined up in it

explanation.surface: A doctor notes that, in this patient, the heartbeat is steady.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulses are edible seeds such as peas; this old word means a pea pod.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for the pod or husk holding peas.

clue.text: One can safely give a child a satisfactory report

definitions.text: One can safely give a child a satisfactory report

parts.words: One can safely give a child a satisfactory report
parts.note: read as a teacher's school report, but a report is also a bang, which a harmless toy weapon makes

explanation.surface: A teacher who can hand a pupil a good school report without worry.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy weapon firing a cork with a loud bang is harmless enough for children.

clue.text: Politic, beginning to prohibit offensive books

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of prohibit is used

parts.note: rude means offensive
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A wise move to begin banning offensive literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Politic as an adjective means wise and sensible, careful in action.

clue.text: Male crocodile swallows retired attorney. FOR example?

indicators.note: swallows means the first two pieces take the next one inside them

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a crocodile is a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the attorney's letters go backwards

parts.note: DA is a district attorney

explanation.surface: A bizarre news story about a crocodile eating a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: A crocodile is the British name for a file of pupils walking two by two. FOR in capitals, a short punchy word, is the sort of thing printed at the top of a news story.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper titles are set in capitals and often use short words, such as FOR, to save space.

clue.text: It contains a pool his nibs may take a dip in

definitions.text: It contains a pool his nibs may take a dip in

parts.words: It contains a pool his nibs may take a dip in
parts.note: read as some grandee's swimming pool, but the pool is ink and the nibs are pen nibs dipped in it

explanation.surface: A grand house whose pool the master might bathe in.
explanation.walkthrough: His nibs is British slang for a self-important man.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pot set into a desk holds the ink a pen dips into.

clue.text: Motivation for newspaper article about motorway being up

indicators.note: being up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards
about means the newspaper's name goes round the motorway

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
the M1 is a British motorway, written MI
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Reasons behind a news story about motorway roadworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being up' reads SUMINA upwards. The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, its 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is the driving spirit or intention behind an action, often hostile.

clue.text: Object of ridicule, but in favourable position with shares

parts.note: to be laughing is to be well placed, sitting pretty
stock is shares in a company

explanation.surface: Someone mocked by all is nonetheless doing nicely from their shareholdings.
explanation.definitionFit: A person everyone mocks becomes a figure of public scorn and derision.

clue.text: Gold that's left in an Oxford college

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
IE is id est, that is

explanation.surface: Gold was left behind in an Oxford college.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel is one of the colleges making up the University of Oxford.

clue.text: Story of young girl speaking with a lisp

indicators.note: speaking with a lisp means the S sound comes out as TH

parts.note: a miss is a young girl

explanation.surface: A tale about a little girl who lisps.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend or traditional tale, often about gods or heroes.

clue.text: From Kent, he takes a letter overseas

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of a run of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man in Kent posts a letter abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The run hides across Kent, he and takes; 'overseas' says the letter belongs to a foreign alphabet. Kent is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet, a foreign letter.

clue.text: Girl crosses ravine to get plant

indicators.note: crosses means the girl's name spans the ravine, holding it inside

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
a chine is a narrow ravine, a word used on the Isle of Wight and in Dorset

explanation.surface: A girl walks across a gorge to reach a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks botanical but means industrial equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant in the industrial sense is the heavy equipment or machines in a works.

clue.text: Crazy about girl providing seasoning

definitions.note: singular, where the answer is the plural of a spice

indicators.note: about means the word for crazy goes round the girl's name

parts.note: nuts means crazy
Meg is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone is mad about a girl who supplies spices.
explanation.definitionFit: The aromatic seeds of an evergreen tree are grated as a spice in cooking.

clue.text: Devious lady originally hailed as temptress

indicators.note: devious means taking a winding course, so the letters are rearranged
originally means only the first letter of lady is used

explanation.surface: A scheming woman was first greeted as a seductress.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible she seduced Samson and betrayed him, so the name means a seductive betrayer.
